summary: Iteration 2 backend testing complete. All 16 new tests for site-settings and cash-flow transactions PASS (100%). Also re-ran iteration 1 suite (14 tests) — all still pass. Coverage: public GET /api/settings, admin PUT /api/settings, unauth 401 + customer 403 guard, admin logo upload/download (multipart PNG, image/* content-type roundtrip), transaction CRUD (income cash / expense card / update / delete) with GET verification and filter checks (kind, method, date_from), and the summary aggregation endpoint (today income=1500 expense=500 net=1000; by_method cash=1500 card=-500; daily_series=7 week_series=4 month_series=6; after update to 2000 → today.income=2000, net=1500, by_method.cash=2000). All 6 auth-guard tests pass (customer 403 for GET/POST transactions, GET summary, PUT settings, POST logo; unauth 401 for GET /transactions and /transactions/summary).

minor.issue: Weekly aggregation uses (year, isoweek) tuple to bucket by week; if 'today' near ISO week boundary this behaves correctly, but the label 'H{week}' does not include the year, so two weeks from adjacent years could share the same label in edge cases (Jan 1 / Dec 31).

Monthly series is computed as `today.replace(day=1) - timedelta(days=30*i)`. Because month lengths vary (28/29/30/31), for i=5 this can drift into the wrong month (e.g. starting in Aug it can accidentally hit July twice, missing a month). Only affects display labeling, not the today/week/month totals which use exact date-prefix matching. Recommend using dateutil.relativedelta or an explicit year/month decrement.
TransactionIn is required as full payload for PUT; there is no PATCH. Not blocking, just noting: partial updates require sending all fields.
Public endpoint returns entire settings doc including internal 'updated_at' and 'logo_id'; considered acceptable but callers should be aware.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1038 lines — even more urgent to split into routers (auth, settings, transactions, gallery, appointments, staff, reports).
GET /api/transactions/summary loads ALL transactions into memory (limit 5000). Fine at MVP scale but should be MongoDB-aggregated ($facet with date-bucketed pipelines) before production growth.

Monthly series calculation using `today.replace(day=1) - timedelta(days=30*i)` is off-by-one prone for months that don't have 30 days — replace with proper month arithmetic (dateutil.relativedelta or explicit y,m decrement).

Route order: /api/transactions/summary is declared AFTER /api/transactions/{tid}. Because HTTP methods differ (GET vs PUT/DELETE) FastAPI matches correctly today, but if a future GET /transactions/{tid} is added it must be declared AFTER /summary or /summary must move up.

PUT /api/settings uses `{k: v for k, v in payload.model_dump().items() if v is not None}` — good; but there's no way to clear a field to empty string (empty string is preserved, None is dropped). Fine for current UI.
put_object/get_object are still synchronous requests.* calls inside async endpoints (branding + gallery + transactions logo). Repeats the concern from iteration 1.
seed_data_creation: Autouse module-scoped fixture cleans today's transactions before AND after the test module runs so summary assertions are deterministic. Test creates TEST_ prefixed customer for guard tests. Settings are mutated to 'Fotuber Test' / '05001112233' then restored to defaults 'Fotuber' / '05010002523'. One logo is uploaded to Emergent object storage under fotuber/branding/logo-<id>.png — not deleted (no delete-logo endpoint exists yet).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Both test suites (backend_test.py + test_settings_transactions.py) are pytest-clean and re-runnable. Pytest requires '-o "addopts="' override because /app/backend/pytest.ini enables xdist by default and xdist reruns cleanup fixtures per worker — running single-worker is more reliable for these order-sensitive summary assertions. Use REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env (test file auto-loads it). Transactions summary is UTC-date-based — assertions use datetime.utcnow().date().isoformat() as TODAY. No delete-logo endpoint yet, so uploaded test logos accumulate in DB.site_assets — harmless.
rca of the issue: No defects found in this iteration.
